title: Stratus Labs - Discovery: migration from OpenAI to Dedicated
summary: Intro discovery call for Stratus Labs evaluation of Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer currently on OpenAI with vLLM inference; main concerns are cost, eval parity, compatibility with TGI/vLLM stack, and security/compliance for PHI. Agreed next steps: share pricing and Dedicated sizing, security whitepaper, and run benchmark with Stratus eval set.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Time: 4:00 PM PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Reyes (Stratus CTO), Liam O'Connor (Stratus ML Eng), Nina Park (Stratus Security)

[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is ava from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with marco and priya from our eng team. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dana Reyes: good thanks, and you?
[00:10] Ava Chen: good — quick agenda, 1) learn about your current infra and goals, 2) compatibility concerns migrating from OpenAI/vLLM, 3) security and deployment options, 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:20] Liam O'Connor: yep that works. to set context, we're running most prod through OpenAI right now, some stuff on Anthropic. recently started using vLLM for inference on our EC2 fleet for lower-cost batch generation. main ask is whether we can move to Redwood Dedicated to control cost and meet residency requirements but without losing eval parity.
[00:38] Marco Silva: thanks — when you say eval parity, can you expand? are you tracking exact metrics and prompts versus OpenAI outputs?
[00:45] Liam O'Connor: yeah we have a couple thousand prompt-response evals — classification-ish and long-form summarization. the concern is that switching runtimes or quantization will change outputs and break downstream QA.
[00:57] Priya Patel: totally understandable. two things we usually do: 1) model catalog mapping — pick an open model that matches OpenAI behavior, or provide Redwood-hosted variants; 2) run an eval parity run with your prompts on our infra and compare diffs. we also support running the same TGI/vLLM optimized weights if you bring them.
[01:15] Dana Reyes: when you say "bring them" do you mean we can take our fine-tuned checkpoints and run on Dedicated?
[01:20] Marco Silva: yes, provided license permits and format is supported — we support standard PyTorch and GGML formats, and we have a model onboarding flow. for vLLM/TGI tensors we can usually ingest the model or recompile it into our runtime. sometimes there are minor tokenization or stopping differences, but we log those and we can knob the stopping behavior.
[01:38] Nina Park: on security, key question: can you integrate with our KMS and maintain logs in our VPC? we have PHI in some prompts so SOC 2 + HIPAA-ish controls are required.
[01:48] Ava Chen: yes. Private deployments support customer-managed KMS and on-prem options. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools with VPC peering and audit logs. we also have SOC 2 and can share artifacts; we'll follow up with the security pack.
[01:59] Liam O'Connor: how about latency — currently our SLO is p95 under 250ms for short prompts. on OpenAI it's pretty fast, but cost is high at scale.
[02:08] Marco Silva: latency is workload-dependent. for low-latency production we recommend pinning to a smaller sequence-optimized model or provisioning Dedicated capacity with fixed concurrency. for example, for a 2k token context, our Dedicated p95 numbers on A100-ish infra are X — we'll run your benchmarks to give real numbers.
[02:26] Dana Reyes: you said "X" — do you have public numbers?
[02:28] Priya Patel: we have benchmark sheets; i'll link them. caveat: numbers vary by model, quantization level, and kernel selection. we do automatic kernel selection and KV cache optimizations to help with multi-request workloads.
[02:40] Liam O'Connor: about vLLM — we rely on batching tricks and custom scheduling in vLLM, will Redwood's runtime support that or will we need to change batching?
[02:49] Marco Silva: our runtime does continuous batching and has workload-aware batching rules. it's not identical to vLLM but conceptually similar; you can tune batch sizes and latency windows. also we have prefix/KV caching which helps for chat-style workloads.
[03:05] Dana Reyes: what about TGI? we use some TGI stacks for serving because it's lightweight — can you run that in Dedicated?
[03:12] Marco Silva: yes we interop with TGI artifacts; we also provide an optimized path in our runtime that often outperforms vanilla TGI. if you want, we can bring your TGI pipeline and run it on Dedicated in a pilot.
[03:24] Nina Park: audit logs — can we route them to our SIEM?
[03:27] Ava Chen: yes, log forwarding to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder in the VPC is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments.
[03:34] Liam O'Connor: curious about upgrade/rollouts — if we pin a model and then Redwood updates kernels, what guarantees are there for stability?
[03:41] Priya Patel: we have rollouts and canary deploys per customer. you control model pinning and a rollout policy; we also have automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if a new kernel impacts performance.
[03:51] Dana Reyes: cost model — can you give roughs? our monthly token spend on OpenAI is ~$85k and growing.
[03:59] Ava Chen: roughly, Dedicated is committed capacity pricing — you get lower per-token unit cost in exchange for committed monthly spend. we also have optimization tooling — quantization suggestions, caching and batching guidance to cut unit cost. i'll send a tailored sizing and pricing deck.
[04:13] Liam O'Connor: one blocker is that some of our prompts need the exact same output to pass legal review. is there a way to do a canary with a double-run approach to compare outputs live?
[04:22] Marco Silva: yes we often do shadowing — you can run requests against Redwood Dedicated in parallel with OpenAI and compare diffs. we can also attach eval tooling to flag regressions automatically.
[04:33] Dana Reyes: timeline — we have a Q2 deadline to reduce OpenAI spend and have a compliance audit in May. realistic?
[04:40] Ava Chen: yes, typical pilot → bench → piloting production in 4–8 weeks, depending on onboarding speed and data access.
[04:47] Nina Park: any gotchas with bringing our fine-tuned models? licensing and tokenizers are big ones for us.
[04:53] Priya Patel: tokenizers can be tricky; we have a tokenizer compatibility matrix. if there's a mismatch we'll either convert tokenizer artifacts or run a token-level mapping. licensing we don't host commercial-only checkpointed models without explicit permissions.
[05:06] Liam O'Connor: do you support private deployment where the control plane is still Redwood but compute is in our VPC?
[05:12] Marco Silva: yes that's our Private option: customer-managed networking, VPC peering, optional on-prem package. control plane can be customer-hosted for air-gapped requirements.
[05:22] Dana Reyes: OK, for next steps can we get a benchmark run and security packet? also want to get their network team into a follow-up call.
[05:29] Ava Chen: yes. action items we'll record.
[05:32] [TRANSCRIPTION NOTE] occasional audio artifact at 00:00-00:05.
[05:35] Marco Silva: quick question — on your vLLM infra, what parts are homegrown vs third-party?
[05:41] Liam O'Connor: we built a custom scheduler around vLLM, prefer to keep that if possible, but we could offload to Redwood if the economics make sense.
[05:49] Priya Patel: we can support hybrid — let us run a pilot to measure economics.
[05:54] Dana Reyes: what's the expected lift for our infra team to do Dedicated?
[05:58] Ava Chen: for Dedicated, minimal lift: we handle provisioning, you provide VPC peering info and credentials for KMS if you want key control. for Private/on-prem it's more involved — we'll coordinate an infra workshop.
[06:13] Liam O'Connor: any SLA numbers?
[06:15] Ava Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for enterprise plans, we'll share specifics in the proposal.
[06:21] Nina Park: does Redwood keep training data or prompts?
[06:24] Priya Patel: by default hosted API retains logs for debugging but enterprise Dedicated can turn off retention or send logs to your retention store. Private keeps control on your side.
[06:34] Dana Reyes: are there cases where model outputs differ substantially when moving from OpenAI to open models even after tuning?
[06:41] Marco Silva: yes — generative models differ. however our eval parity workflow surfaces those diffs and we can tune system prompts or recommend a different model/quantization level to match behavior. sometimes you need slight prompt rework.
[06:57] Liam O'Connor: can we run an initial eval on a sample of 500 prompts?
[06:59] Ava Chen: absolutely — that's a good size to start. we'll need the prompts and target criteria.
[07:04] Dana Reyes: what about data residency — some EU customers require data not leave EU. do you have region-specific Dedicated clusters?
[07:11] Ava Chen: yes we have regions and Dedicated clusters by region; for strict residency we recommend Private deployments within the region.
[07:18] Marco Silva: technically we can pin model versions and kernels to a region.
[07:22] Liam O'Connor: sample diffs would be great — like a diff report.
[07:25] Priya Patel: we produce a report showing token-level diff, rouge/bleu-ish metrics for summarization, plus a human pass if you want.
[07:33] Dana Reyes: ok let's talk next steps.
[07:36] Ava Chen: i'll summarize: 1) Ava sends Dedicated sizing and pricing + public benchmarks; 2) Priya shares security pack (SOC 2, KMS integration docs); 3) Stratus to provide 500-sample eval set and acceptance criteria; 4) schedule bench run week of 3/9; 5) intro to network/security team for a follow-up. anyone want to modify?
[07:56] Dana Reyes: that's accurate.
[07:58] Liam O'Connor: one more on cost — can you give an estimate of the commit for similar throughput?
[08:03] Ava Chen: we'll include a couple sizing scenarios: light (shadowing + low prod), medium (partial prod), heavy (full prod).
[08:12] [15:00] Marco Silva: (deep dive) for the bench we'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens under your workload; also show quantization experiments (fp16 vs int8).
[15:21] Liam O'Connor: do you have customers who've moved from OpenAI to Dedicated and stayed within tolerance?
[15:26] Priya Patel: yes, several enterprise customers migrated with ~<5% eval drift after prompt tuning and small re-runs. we can anonymize case studies.
[15:35] Nina Park: data retention for debug logs — can we redact PHI automatically?
[15:40] Marco Silva: we support automated redaction rules and custom filters before logs leave your VPC.
[20:05] Dana Reyes: what's the expected onboarding time for us to be production-ready?
[20:10] Ava Chen: usually 4–8 weeks; pilot 1–2 weeks to get bench results.
[28:12] Priya Patel: technical note — quantization can change hallucination patterns; we recommend metric-driven checks during quantization experiments.
[31:45] Liam O'Connor: ok after the bench, what's the rollback plan if outputs degrade in prod?
[31:50] Marco Silva: rollback to pinned model version or fallback to hosted variant (OpenAI or Redwood-hosted) if you set a hybrid routing policy; we advise canarying new models before full rollout.
[37:20] Ava Chen: any final questions?
[37:25] Dana Reyes: none from me — thanks.
[37:28] Liam O'Connor: nope, good call.
[37:30] Nina Park: thanks everyone.
[37:33] Ava Chen: great, we'll follow up with notes and the packet. thanks all.
[41:20] Call ends.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional mis-attributed speaker labels and a minor audio artifact at start.
